statements: The deadline for sending the Commission's accounts to the Auditor General is set by section 21(2) of the Public Finance and Accountability (Scotland) Act 2000, which requires the account to be sent not later than 6 months after the end of the financial year to which it relates.

The Water Industry (Scotland) Act 2002 does not itself fix that deadline: paragraph 14 of schedule A1 requires the Commission to send its account to the Auditor General for Scotland by such time as the Scottish Ministers may direct.

Section 5(1)(a) of the Water Industry (Scotland) Act 2002 requires the Commission, as soon as practicable after the end of each financial year, to submit to the Scottish Ministers and publish a report on the exercise of its functions during that year.

Paragraph 14 of schedule A1 to the Water Industry (Scotland) Act 2002 requires the Commission to prepare an account of its income and expenditure for each financial year in accordance with directions given by the Scottish Ministers.

The auditor's report on the account must set out the auditor's findings on the matters listed in section 22 of the Public Finance and Accountability (Scotland) Act 2000, including whether the expenditure and receipts shown were incurred or applied in accordance with the enactments and Budget Acts that authorised them.
